structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, then in a species-level mammal phylogeny Perissodactyla and Leporidae share a more recent common ancestor with each other than Perissodactyla share with Artiodactyla (the other ungulates), and than Leporidae share with other Rodentia.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In at least 95% of the posterior trees, the MRCA of Perissodactyla (Equidae, Rhinocerotidae, Tapiridae) and Leporidae is younger than both (a) the MRCA of Perissodactyla and Artiodactyla and (b) the MRCA of Leporidae and Rodentia. Equivalently, the Perissodactyla+Leporidae clade excludes Artiodactyla and Rodentia.
structured_output.fail_criterion: In at least 50% of the posterior trees, the MRCA of Leporidae and Rodentia is younger than the MRCA of Leporidae and Perissodactyla. Alternatively, the MRCA of Perissodactyla and Artiodactyla is younger than that of Perissodactyla and Leporidae. Either result refutes the claim. Between the two thresholds the claim is not supported.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'more closely related' is read as cladistic recency of common ancestry, meaning a sister-group or nearer-node relationship. It is not read as morphological similarity of the skull. 'Other Ungulates' is operationalised as Artiodactyla. 'Rest of the Rodentia' is operationalised as Rodentia. Thompson's claim concerns the rabbit and the rhinoceros skull. A modern molecular phylogeny tests the inference of relatedness, not the geometric transformation itself. Modern expectation: Lagomorpha is sister to Rodentia (Glires), and Perissodactyla is nested in Laurasiatheria, so the claim is expected to fail.

dataset.name: Mammal trees (Inferring the mammal tree: species-level sets of phylogenies for questions in ecology, evolution, and conservation), VertLife
dataset.why_it_fits: It provides downloadable sets of Newick posterior trees covering about 5,900 mammal species, including Equidae, Rhinocerotidae, Tapiridae, Leporidae, Artiodactyla and Rodentia. The test uses the tip labels and branch lengths to compute, per tree, the MRCA node ages for Perissodactyla+Leporidae, Perissodactyla+Artiodactyla and Leporidae+Rodentia, and the fraction of trees satisfying each ordering.
